ai.summary: The trust gate now treats MCP servers listed by a remote agent template as executable content, refusing unpublished publisher templates that define them unless the publisher is trusted. `fetchAgentFromDatabase` validates the publisher, agent, and version segments against `PUBLISHED_ID_SEGMENT` and `PUBLISHED_VERSION` before building the registry URL, blocking ids that could rewrite the path. eli5.text: The trust check for downloadable agents now also covers agents that connect to external tools (MCP servers): a remote agent from a publisher you haven't approved will be refused if it lists external tools or executable program code, not just if it includes custom code. The agent address is also checked before the request is sent, so a crafted publisher, agent, or version name can no longer redirect the lookup to a different agent on the registry. This closes a gap where pulling anyone's public agent could silently spawn external processes or connect to outside tools on your machine. Internal tooling change with no direct effect on end users unless they run ad-hoc remote agents, in which case untrusted ones that reach out to external servers or code will now be blocked by default.

ai.title: Filter unreliable timezone signals from Freebucks scheduling header
ai.summary: The timezone resolution in `common/src/util/freebucks-timezone.ts` now delegates to `freebucksDeviceTimeZone` to prevent a server-side image default or ICU quirk from overwriting an account's schedule. This change adds a `FreebucksTimeZoneRuntime` interface and `isRemoteHost` detection to omit `x-fb-timezone` when the user is on a remote host, when the `TZ` environment variable causes Bun to answer UTC incorrectly, or when a Windows machine reports a fixed-offset zone instead of a named one. Two environment variables, `REMOTE_CONTAINERS` and `GITPOD_WORKSPACE_ID`, are newly included in the remote-host check so that development containers also drop the header rather than send a misleading UTC default.
ai.evidence: In `common/src/util/freebucks-timezone.ts`, the diff replaces the inline timezone resolution in `freebucksTimeZoneHeaders` with the new `freebucksDeviceTimeZone` function, adding the `FreebucksTimeZoneRuntime` type and `isRemoteHost` checks to filter out false UTC or Windows `Etc/GMT±N` values.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show the corresponding server-side ingestion logic for the `x-fb-timezone` header, which determines how a missing header affects the account's schedule versus a provided one.

changes.what: Introduces `FreebucksTimeZoneRuntime`, `isRemoteHost`, and `freebucksDeviceTimeZone` to filter out erroneous timezone signals from remote hosts and Windows. This updates `freebucksTimeZoneHeaders` to return an empty object instead of a UTC header when the device's zone is unreliable.

eli5.text: The free coding assistant now leaves out its timezone guess when it is running in a remote environment, such as a development container or over a secure connection, because those systems often report a default setting rather than your actual location. It also withholds the time zone when your computer is set to a specific, non-naming offset that does not match your other devices, or when the underlying system cannot confidently identify your location. testNames: a crashed writer no longer prevents deleting a saved connection
recovery preserves a live owner even when its lock is old
competing processes recover a legacy PID lock without losing writes
throwing from an operation releases its lock for the next writer

facts: Publish an already-complete PID atomically. Creating an empty lock and then writing its owner leaves an unrecoverable lock if killed between.
EPERM (including another user's process) is not evidence of death.
Recover PID locks without allowing two reapers to unlink a successor's lock.

A second filesystem lock would itself survive a crash. A loopback listener is a short-lived, kernel-released reaper mutex on every supported OS. Key it by the observed PID, so aliases of the configuration path share the mutex. Collisions only defer recovery; they never allow concurrent reapers.
Re-read under the mutex: another reaper may already have removed the old lock and a writer may now own the pathname. Never expire a live PID by age.

ai.title: BYOK lock recovery via PID check and loopback mutex
ai.summary: The BYOK metadata store lock in `sdk/src/byok.ts` now writes a PID to a candidate file and atomically links it to `connections.lock`, preventing stale empty locks that previously required manual deletion after a crash. The new `sdk/src/impl/byok-lock.ts` module provides `recoverByokLock`, which verifies a lock owner is dead using `process.kill` and a short-lived loopback TCP listener to serialize concurrent reapers. This prevents multiple processes from simultaneously unlinking a successor's lock file while ensuring live PIDs are never expired by age.
ai.evidence: The diff replaces the file-handle lock in `sdk/src/byok.ts` `createBunByokMetadataStore.withLock` with an atomic PID file and hard link, and adds `sdk/src/impl/byok-lock.ts` which exports `recoverByokLock` to verify owner liveness via `process.kill` and a loopback TCP mutex.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not specify which OS versions are supported for the loopback listener strategy or how the CLI surface reports the new lock timeout behavior to users.
